title: COMO: Closed-Loop Optical Molecule Recognition with Minimum Risk Training
abstract: arXiv:2604.23546v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Optical chemical structure recognition (OCSR) translates molecular images into machine-readable representations such as SMILES strings or molecular graphs, but remains challenging in real-world documents due to wide variations in chemical structures, shorthand conventions, and scanning artifacts. Most existing deep learning approaches rely on teacher forcing with token-level Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE). This training paradigm suffers from exposure bias, as models are trained under ground-truth prefixes but must condition on their own previous predictions during inference. Moreover, token-level MLE objectives hinder the optimization towards molecular-level evaluation criteria such as chemical validity and structural similarity. Here we introduce Minimum Risk Training (MRT) to OCSR and propose COMO (Closed-loop Optical Molecule recOgnition), a framework that mitigates exposure bias by directly optimizing over molecule-lev

translated_title: COMO：基于最小风险训练的闭环光学分子识别
translated_abstract: 光学化学结构识别（OCSR）旨在将分子图像转换为SMILES字符串或分子图等机器可读的表示形式，但由于化学结构变化多样、存在简写约定以及扫描伪影等因素，其在真实世界文档中的应用仍然极具挑战性。大多数现有的深度学习方法依赖于采用token级最大似然估计（MLE）的教师强制训练范式。这种训练范式存在暴露偏差问题，因为模型在训练时使用的是真实值前缀，而在推理时却必须以自身先前的预测结果为条件。此外，token级的MLE目标函数难以针对化学有效性和结构相似性等分子级评估指标进行优化。在此，我们将最小风险训练引入OCSR领域，并提出了COMO（闭环光学分子识别）框架，该框架通过直接在分子级上进行优化来缓解暴露偏差……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出COMO框架，首次将最小风险训练引入光学化学结构识别任务，通过在分子级进行闭环直接优化来缓解暴露偏差，从而更好地优化化学有效性和结构相似性等分子级评估指标。
